segments.text: I stumbled into the weirdest thing recently,  and it all starts with this little pill...
“Researchers discover some very exciting new  benefits of a drug already on the market…”
“Metformin”
“metformin”
“metformin”
“The first anti-aging drug..."
"Possible anti-aging drug..."
"Can you spell it? M-E-T...
"Could be revolutionary!"
"Is it really the fountain of youth? Are we onto something here?"
This isn't some sketchy supplement.
It’s a real drug! It’s been used effectively  by people with diabetes for decades
to control their blood sugar.
And it's cheap! It's really cheap.
It's pennies per pill.
It’s all in the news now because it's getting popular with another group of people
with a lot of money, for a different purpose.
So… to try to live longer, billionaires  are taking a pill that costs pennies.
Does it... work??
DR. NIR BARZILAI: This is important...
Anti-aging generally has a bad name. In anti-aging there are lots of charlatans.
“What are you selling, mister? Snake oil?”
“I tell you Mother, we’re cheating  all the people, don’t you see?”
BARZILAI: "You'll take this  and you live forever."And if they die,
nobody sues them, right?
So those are our enemy.
That’s Dr. Nir Barzilai. He’s the person you call
if you have serious questions about aging.
And he answered my first one right away...
We're not talking about a...
“fountain of youth”
"The fountain of youth"
“The fountain of youth!”
“You found no fountain of youth here!”
BARZILAI: The thing that is not happening is
taking an old person and making young, okay?
Sorry. What researchers are actually trying to do is
figure out if there's any way we can delay the effects of aging.
And I don’t mean wrinkles and gray hair.
I mean about the chance you die.
As you age, the chance you die goes up.
Specifically, the chance you die from  these very common diseases goes up.
Why does the chance of dying from cancer,  heart disease, Alzheimer's go up with age?
BARZILAI: We're thinking wrong about  it. It's the biology of aging that
drives the disease. And if you stop this  biology of aging, you stop this disease.
What he told me, and this took me a minute to wrap  my head around, is that: Our bodies accumulate
damage as time goes on. The diseases most of  us die from spring from that damage - often in
ways we don’t totally understand.
But if you could delay the damage somehow,
you could also delay the diseases, right? And  make it more likely you survive for longer.
And in 2014, Dr. Barzilai happened on the  results of a very interesting study…
BARZILAI: This is a study from the UK where  they took 180,000 people approximately…
They looked at three groups of people:  People with diabetes taking metformin,
people with diabetes taking other drugs  not metformin, and people without diabetes
who weren’t taking any diabetes drugs.
The people with diabetes who weren't taking metformin had
double the mortality - the number of  deaths - than the people without diabetes.
BARZILAI: But this is really what was cool: People  on metformin that were diabetics, were more obese,
they were more sick to begin with, had less  mortality than people without diabetes.
The fact that people with  diabetes who were taking metformin
died less than people WITHOUT diabetes is HUGE.
But if you're applying that to anti-aging, there are some really big caveats:
First: These are correlations. This is a retrospective study.
They’re looking back at what happened,
they weren't able to test whether metformin CAUSED it to happen.
And second, the only people taking metformin in this study were people with diabetes.
It’s not clear whether that whole “dying less” thing
applies to people without diabetes.
And at this point, you might be wondering
“how does it even work?”
Well, we know a lot about  how metformin works in people with diabetes:
When you eat or drink, your blood transports  sugars to your cells to use as fuel.
In people with diabetes, these blood sugar levels  can get too high and metformin helps control that.
We have research on this going back decades to  before metformin was first approved.
We know a lot less about how it may or may not  work in people without diabetes for anti-aging.
One reason for that is, these days, it’s  already a cheap generic drug, which means
there’s not as much incentive for pharmaceutical  companies to do expensive new research.
Other studies show metformin does seem  to have anti-aging effects in healthy
mice and worms. Which is interesting…
But to know for sure whether metformin can actually delay
aging in most people, we need more research.
That’s what Dr. Barzilai is trying to do.
"Dr. Barzilai is about to launch a new nationwide study!"
"A proper randomized trial where they give half the people metformin
and half the people a placebo drug..."
"So you're going to be hearing a lot more about this in the future!"
BARZILAI: This is really the challenge  that I'm leading now. This is the TAME study.
TAME stands for Targeting Aging with Metformin.  And the reason I’m doing that is not to repeat
the studies that I told you! It’s to really  plan a study for the FDA to repurpose a drug
that we believe targets aging.
It’s hard to overstate how incredible
this would be if it works.
They’re trying to figure out if
aging is treatable.
if something can push back the accumulation of damage,
and push back the diseases that kill the most of us.
And if that “something” isn’t some crazy million-dollar thing
but a drug that is already on the market and  already affordable for many, many people.
I get surprisingly emotional  thinking about this topic.
"That!"
"That! Is a camera!"
Really, I...
genuinely can’t think of anything that I would want  more than more time with the people I love.
In the meantime, whether or not you wanna  take metformin or I do boils down to our
assessment of 3 different factors:
The first is, what you think of the existing studies
(not the TAME trial, because  it probably won’t be done for a while)
The second is how urgent aging actually feels  to you. That’s a very personal choice.
The third is how you weigh your perceived  benefits against the side effects…
BARZILAI: There's very common side effects in  the first week of use. You feel early satiety,
you're not hungry. You might have kind of  upset stomach. You might have diarrhea.
It also impacts how your body  responds to exercise.
BARZILAI: When you exercise with or without  metformin, your muscle will have the same
increased capacity, but the  muscle wouldn't be as big.
Ok. Would I have diarrhea for a  week and be less good at exercise
if I could live 5 years longer? Yes. Absolutely.
Would I opt in for that if I weren’t pretty sure it would work?
No, probably not.
So the people in the news right now who are taking metformin
for anti-aging, without  diabetes, are making a specific calculation:
“We don’t want to wait for more studies,  we’re happy with the studies we have.
We don’t mind these side effects too much, and aging  feels pretty urgent. We’re getting older.”
You know, I’ve been struggling a little bit  as a journalist working on this piece.
Because on the one hand, I really want to present information that experts tell me
is important and valuable for the future.
And on the other hand, I really don’t  want anyone to go take a medication
because they watched a YouTube video!
I personally don’t take metformin,
that’s how my calculation came out. I want to wait for more studies.
But metformin isn’t the only option being studied.
Researchers are looking at more  and more drugs for anti-aging effects.
If we figure out that any option meaningfully delays the effects of aging in most people
that is too huge to ignore or scoff at.
18 million people die of heart disease every year.
10 million people die of cancer.
55 million people have  Alzheimers or other dementias.
Some of those people are in my family,
NONNA: "It's a perfect picture of him..."
are my loved ones.
Some, I imagine, are yours.
And I can’t help but imagine
what I would do
with more time.
